name: お好み焼 みっちゃん総本店 八丁堀本店 (Okonomiyaki Mitchan Sohonten Hatchobori Hont)

claims.text: Okonomiyaki is cooked on a shared teppan griddle where wheat batter, wheat noodles, and wheat-based sauce are prepared together, making wheat cross-contact unavoidable.
The signature okonomiyaki sauce is a wheat-based sauce; standard Japanese okonomiyaki/soy seasonings contain wheat.
Dishes contain egg, pork, fish-based dashi, oysters and offal, all cooked on the same shared teppan; no vegan preparation is documented.

name: お好み焼き ももちゃん（百々商店） (Okonomiyaki Momochan (Momo Shoten))

claims.text: All okonomiyaki here are built on a wheat-flour batter and wheat noodles cooked on a shared teppan griddle, so cross-contamination with gluten is unavoidable.
Hiroshima okonomiyaki is finished with a sweet okonomiyaki sauce that typically contains wheat; no wheat-free sauce is indicated.
Dishes are cooked on a shared griddle alongside pork, egg, oysters, and fish (anago/chikuwa), so vegan-safe preparation is not possible here.

name: お好み焼 もり (Okonomiyaki Mori)

claims.text: Cooked on a shared teppan grill where wheat-batter okonomiyaki and wheat noodles are prepared; no gluten-free handling is mentioned.
Uses a sweet okonomiyaki-style sauce (described as a 大福ソース-type sauce), which is wheat-based and not gluten-free.
Single shared teppan used for pork, egg, squid and noodles; no separate vegan preparation indicated.

name: お好み焼 長田屋 (Okonomiyaki Nagata-ya)

claims.text: Hiroshima okonomiyaki is assembled on a shared communal teppan and built on wheat batter plus wheat noodles, so there is no gluten-free preparation path and high cross-contact for celiac diners.
Standard okonomiyaki sauce contains wheat; the menu does not break out sauce ingredients, so wheat should be assumed in the regular sauce.

Vegan and vegetarian okonomiyaki are cooked on the same teppan used for pork, egg, and oyster dishes, so strict vegans should be aware of shared-surface cross-contact even though the recipes themselves are animal-free.

English menus and English-speaking staff are available, and dedicated plant-based menus are provided on request, which helps with communicating dietary needs, though no formal allergen protocol is documented.
Offers genuine dedicated vegan and vegetarian okonomiyaki using an animal-free special sauce, with vegetables replacing the usual pork and egg.
Plant-based diners can eat the city's signature dish here with English-language support, a rare accommodation among Hiroshima okonomiyaki shops.

name: お好み焼き 桜まる (Okonomiyaki Sakuramaru)

claims.text: Wheat-based okonomiyaki batter and wheat noodles are cooked on a shared teppan griddle alongside all dishes, so a gluten-free meal is not feasible here.
No allergen labeling is published; okonomiyaki sauce and seasonings are standardly wheat-containing and no gluten-free alternative is documented.
Oysters, pork, egg and other seafood are central to the menu and share the same griddle; no vegan preparation is documented.
An English menu is available, which can help a traveler ask about ingredients.

name: お好み焼・鉄板焼 八誠 (Okonomiyaki Teppanyaki Hassei)

claims.text: Hiroshima okonomiyaki is cooked on a shared teppan griddle that continuously handles wheat batter and wheat noodles, so heavy gluten cross-contact is inherent; no gluten-free protocol is documented.
Dishes use standard okonomi sauce and soy sauce, both typically wheat-containing; no wheat-free sauce is mentioned.
Vegetable teppanyaki items are cooked on the same griddle used for pork, egg, oysters and butter, so vegan/vegetarian dishes are not prepared in isolation.
An English menu with detailed explanations is reported, which makes it easier for foreign visitors to ask about ingredients and choose among the well-stocked vegetable dishes.

name: お好み焼き・鉄板焼き 蔵屋 本店 (Okonomiyaki Teppanyaki Kuraya Honten)

claims.text: Okonomiyaki is made on a shared teppan griddle with a wheat-flour batter and wheat-based crepe layer; the same surface cooks noodles, meat and seafood, so gluten cross-contact is unavoidable.
Teppanyaki and okonomiyaki here use standard wheat-based okonomi sauce and regular soy sauce; no wheat-free or tamari soy sauce is documented.
The teppan is shared with meat, oysters and other seafood, and okonomiyaki normally contains egg, pork and a fish-based sauce, so vegan separation is not available.

name: お好み焼き・鉄板焼き そり家 (Okonomiyaki Teppanyaki Soriya)

claims.text: Hiroshima okonomiyaki is layered on a wheat-flour crepe with wheat noodles and finished with wheat/soy-based sauce, all cooked on one shared teppan griddle, so cross-contact with gluten is unavoidable.
Okonomiyaki/teppanyaki seasoning relies on wheat-containing okonomiyaki and soy sauces typical of Hiroshima-style cooking.
Egg, pork, and fish-based ingredients are cooked on the same shared griddle as all dishes.
